items.stem: Why does Elasticsearch use an inverted index for full-text search?

options.text: It maps each term to the documents containing it, making term lookups fast
options.rationale: Correct: the inverted index lets search jump straight to matching documents per term.

options.text: It stores documents in insertion order for sequential scans
options.rationale: Sequential scanning is what the inverted index avoids.

options.text: It enforces a fixed relational schema
It compresses documents to save disk only
options.rationale: Its purpose is fast term lookup, not primarily compression.

items.explanation: Correct: the inverted index lets search jump straight to matching documents per term.

items.stem: Which statements about text vs keyword fields are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: text fields are analyzed and suited to full-text match queries
options.rationale: Correct: text fields are tokenized for relevance-based matching.

options.text: keyword fields are stored as-is and suited to exact match, sorting and aggregations
options.rationale: Correct: keyword fields are not analyzed, so they aggregate and sort reliably.

options.text: You should aggregate on analyzed text fields by default
options.rationale: Aggregating on analyzed text is discouraged and often disabled.

options.text: term queries on a text field match the original untokenized string
options.rationale: term matches exact tokens, so it often fails on analyzed text.

items.explanation: Correct: text fields are tokenized for relevance-based matching.; Correct: keyword fields are not analyzed, so they aggregate and sort reliably.

items.stem: What is the benefit of placing an exact-match clause in filter context rather than query context?

options.text: It skips relevance scoring and can be cached, improving performance
options.rationale: Correct: filters answer yes/no, are cacheable and do not compute a score.

options.text: It increases the relevance score of matches
options.rationale: Filter context does not contribute to scoring.

options.text: It forces a full re-index of the data
options.rationale: Filter context has nothing to do with re-indexing.

options.text: It converts the field to a text field
options.rationale: Query context does not change field mappings.

items.explanation: Correct: filters answer yes/no, are cacheable and do not compute a score.
